The Price of Press Freedom

By: Julian Sun | Paid

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
What happens when the court system in South Africa is abused to harass journalists, to prevent them from speaking truth to power in an attempt to intimidate them into submission?

Unique Selling Point:
The bill of rights is the cornerstone of South Africa’s democracy. It protects and affirms the values of human dignity, equality and freedom, providing the foundation for the rule of law in this country. Enshrined is the freedom of expression and by extension, the freedom of the press.

But what happens when our venerated judicial system, one that is supposed to uphold and protect this inalienable right, is instead weaponised to do the exact opposite?

This story looks at 2 powerful case studies showing the exactly how this was done, the personal toll it’s taken on the lives of the journalists involved and the consequences on media freedom in South Africa


Summary:
Karyn Maughn is one of South Africa’s most respected journalists
Former President Jacob Zuma launched a private prosecution against her in October - an example of a SLAPP Suit
Zuma’s lawyer Dali Mpofu admitted that they did not really have a case but still chose to launch it anyway -Karyn can provide this clip to us
If found guilty, she faced up to 15 years in prison
The litigation was really expensive. She would not have been able to afford legal representation without the support of News 24 -who supported her throughout and paid for legal counsel.
Her editor Pieter Du Toit is a powerful support interview for her story
She’s been put through 7 months of hell - the target of a vicious social media campaign against her
This led her to withdraw from society, fearing for her safety
She left her home and moved back in with her elderly parents for 2 months
She’s willing to discuss the mental toll it’s taken on her: she’s no longer the extroverted person she used to be
The stress really affected her blood sugar: she’s a type 1 diabetic
The case against her was ultimately dismissed in a scathing judgement against Zuma in which he was ordered to pay legal costs too
Despite the victory, the intimidation and harassment still continues, as evidenced when she was attacked again by Dali Mpofu at Busisiwe Mkhwebane’s press conference
Karyn is willing to admit that in spite of her stoic defence that the ordeal has broken her. She once thought that admitting this would mean that her intimidators had won
It’s become all too much for Karyn and she’s going to Denver for a few weeks to escape and recharge. She’s due back on the 18th July


Amabhungane is a preeminent investigative unit in SA headed up by veteran journalist Sam Sol
They ran a series of exposes on Zunaid Moti’s businesses call the #MotiFiles. These exposes were authored by Dewald Pretorious and Micah Reddy - with Sam acting as a mentor
They based their reporting on a number of sources, including a trove of documents that the Moti Group claim to have been stolen
In written correspondence from the Moti Group, Amabhungane’s journalists are accused of using stolen documents and threatened with criminal prosecution if they do not return them.
At the beginning of June Moti was able to successfully interdict Amabhungane from publishing anymore exposes as well as ordering them to return the “stolen documents”
What’s highly unusual is that the order was obtained “ex parte” - meaning the court order was given without knowledge of AmaBhungane
Amabhungane argue that returning the documents would reveal their source
The case will now be heard in the Johannesburg High Court on Tuesday 27 June.
Sam Sole has been subject of a smear campaign launched on Social Media by Zunaid Moti in which he is accused of being an Apartheid spy.
His family has been harassed. For example his wife was contacted by a lady claiming to be a journalist and asked about Sam’s time in the army. The “journalist” turned out to be someone working for the Moti Group.
Sam, Micah & Dewald have been warned that they face imminent arrest. They fear that Moti has connections with the Sandton Police- though this remains unsubstantiated
This feeling of paranoia has led to several occasions in which they’ve had to hurriedly leave home
The legal persecution by Moti is another example of SLAPP but Amabhungane don’t have the financial resource like News24 and so could buried by litigation and face the real prospect of bankruptcy.

Press Release:


When former President Jacob Zuma accused senior state prosecutor Billy Downer of leaking confidential medical information to journalist Karyn Maughan, she couldn’t have imagined how severely it would impact her life. For several months, Zuma pursued a private prosecution of both, placing Maughan in the crosshairs of some of the former president’s staunchest supporters. In court, Downer and Maughan emerged victorious. But she endured such violent online vitriol that she was forced to retreat to her family home. As a journalist, she’s not alone. It seems South Africa’s judiciary is being used as a battleground to harass and intimidate journalists and prevent them from doing their work. Carte Blanche examines how media freedom is under attack.

Script:


PRESSING ISSUES

PROLOGUE
OPENING LINK Press Freedom is the cornerstone of a healthy democracy. For journalists working in a country like South Africa, we know just how precious that freedom is.

1 V/O: Now, after 30 years of democracy, the media freedom that underpins it appears under threat

UPS KARYN: I just felt like someone had punched me in the guts
UPS MICAH: We were looking at potentially costly legal battles and the very real threat of being locked up.

2 V/O: It’s been an unusually tense few months for a number of journalists, as they face unprecedented interference from some rich and powerful people they report on.

UPS PETER DU TOIT: They don't want South Africans to know what they get up to behind closed doors in the shadows.

DIP TO BLACK - FADE OUT MUSIC

ACT 1 - THE INTIMIDATION
KARYN
KARYN MAKES COFFEE AND SITS DOWN IN HER LOUNGE

3 V/O: Senior legal journalist Karyn Maughan has been covering the legal battles of former president Jacob Zuma for almost two decades.

Karyn: From the time that I started the case. I think I'm the last reporter left that has covered this case consistently.

4 V/O: Zuma’s been fighting corruption charges since 2005 - and now he was coming for Karyn all because of a story she’d written. He accused state prosecutor Adv Billy Downer of leaking a confidential medical document to her, which she used as the basis for the piece.

Karyn: I received notification from a lawyer representing the former president and this young woman called me and said, We need to know your address so we can serve a summons on you. And I felt sick.
Masa: I just got goosebumps as you said that
Karyn: I literally felt ill and I just felt like someone had punched me in the guts.
5 V/O:If found guilty, she faced a maximum sentence of 15 years in jail. -
PAUSE - SEGUE TO THE OFFICE - ESTABLISH PIETER
6. Karyn turned to assistant news editor Pieter du Toit for advise.
Pieter: We absolutely had to defend Karen, who was only doing her job. If we let Karen hang out to dry, we would have betrayed not only our profession, but we would have betrayed democracy.
Karyn: I And he said to me, They don't get your, address Everything goes through the lawyers.
STEVEN BUDLENDER SC - NEWS 24: Jacob Zuma’s attempt..
7. V/O: With News24’s legal team behind her, she’d take the fight to Zuma in the high court
MICAH
8. V/O: Across town…a small investigative team faced a massive legal challenge of their own…for daring to report on well-connected businessman Zunaid Moti. For over a decade AmaBhungane’s garnered a reputation for hard-hitting exposes by investigative journalists like Micah Reddy.
UPSOUND OF MICAH AT DESK ON PHONE

Micah 1: [00:00:50] Can you just give me a, uh, a quick kind of briefing on that?

9 V/O: An anonymous source leaked thousands of confidential documents that formed the basis for a series of exposes dubbed #The Moti Files

Micah: [00:08:42] A lot of what was in those documents pointed to an improper relationship with the Zimbabwean president and potential fraud and corruption in other areas [00:10:13][27.9] … So these are some of the things that we've explored and there's a lot more to come. [00:11:32][32.9]

10 V/O: Before publishing, AmaBhungane offered the Moti group the right to respond to their allegations. Moti and the Group denied any wrongdoing. They also accused amaBhungane of being in possession of stolen documents.

MICAH: We thought they were trying to get at who our source was. And they kept insisting that we hand over the documents. And of course, we wouldn't do that. Source confidentiality is a fundamental principle of journalism.

ZUNAID MOTI: It’s important for you to understand that AmaBhungane are liars, they’re part of a theft and they’re trying to cover it up using tabloids that they leaked to

11 V/O: Their refusal to hand back the documents enraged Zunaid Moti.

12 V/O: In June he escalated the fight when they asked a judge to gag AmaBhungane from publishing further exposes. Not only was the request granted, but they were told to return the documents within 48 hours…and shockingly, it all happened “ex parte”.

Masa: [00:26:19] What does it mean that it was granted ex parte? [00:26:21][2.2]

Micah: [00:26:22] It means that the Moti group went to court secretively without us even knowing and without us being allowed to even present our arguments.

Micah: [00:24:39] It was pretty unprecedented in democratic South Africa because it amounts to pre-publication censorship. It's censorship outright

13. V/O: The Moti Group argued that an ex parte interdict was a common mechanism to secure stolen documents ..they argued that AmaBhungane contradicted themselves on whether they in fact had the documents. But for Anton Harber from the Campaign for Free Expression it was a clear example of SLAPP Suit.

Anton: [00:14:58] SLAPP stands for strategic litigation against public participation. It's the name that’s been given for cases where the intention is not to seek justice or even to win the case, but to make life difficult for journalists or critics of any sort

Anton: [00:03:10] journalists must, in the public interest be able to use leaks that come to them and that the idea of of hearing a case like this ex-parte was outrageous

14. V/O:Amabhungane challenged the ex parte order in the high court. Only time would tell if they or Moti would prevail.

ACT 2 - THE EMOTIONAL TOLL
KARYN

Dip to black
TRANSITION TO KARYN ON COUCH TALKING ON PHONE .. (Reestablishing her at home)
UPS NATOUND: Karyn phone call: [00:04:16] I've got to come to that News 24 event on the Friday night. Do you know what that's about?
Karyn: I had a lot of anxiety, a lot of sort of paralyzing fear. I mean, I got so many threats on social media, “You must be raped and murdered and die, bitch, die”, you know, all that kind of stuff.

Masa: [00:07:57] After that summons was issued. How did your life change? [00:08:01][3.3]

Karyn: [00:08:03] I used to walk into that courtroom in Pietermaritzburg. I've been going there for years as a reporter, and suddenly I had to get bodyguards.

I went to my parents. My parents are both very elderly, and my mom is visually impaired. And I said she had to ask my. Sorry, guys. Um, essentially my, my, my parents were kind of looking off to me, you know? And I'm in my forties. I'm a Type one diabetic. It played havoc with my diabetes. I was going into comas, which my parents had to pull me out of.
Cutaways of Karyn injecting Insulin and taking her blood sugar
Karyn: [00:14:46] Even now, like I walk out in the street and I think a car is going to run me over or, you know, if I if I feel people behind me, I think they're going to shoot me in the head. It's completely unnatural and paranoid and crazy.
MICAH
SEGUE VISUALLY BACK TO MICAH .. INTO VIZ OF LETTER/AUDIO OF THREAT
15. V/O: Karyn wasn’t the only journalist feeling threatened.

Micah and Nicole having Coffee sequence - let’s try cut it slightly longer

16. V/O: For Micah, the fear of arrest took a toll not just on him but his young family too.

Nicole: [00:03:10] But that whole thing from about April when we had to clear out of the house because of security threats and concerns, that’s all been a bit much I think

Micah: [00:27:50] we did think there was a very real risk of arrest. Our lawyers had cautioned us.

Micah: [00:02:03 nerve-wracking precisely because you were worried not only about your own safety but those of that of people around you.
Dip to Black

ACT 3 - THE VERDICT

17. V/O: The anxiety was overwhelming as judgement in these two cases loomed…

We see Micah Driving

Upsound: The Moti Group and AmaBhungane are headed for a legal showdown

We see Karyn leaving her house and on her phone

Up Sound: Judgement will be handed down today in the private prosecution case against journalist Karyn Maughan

18. V/O:. At stake not just Karyn’s personal liberty but nothing less than the future of media freedom in South Africa.

KARYN
Karyn: [00:16:51] Did I ever think that the former president was going to try and put me in jail for 15 years for doing my job? No, I didn't.
Karyn: [00:15:39] What I did think astounding was the former president's lawyers telling a court that using court documents to report was somehow potentially worse than murder,
Anton: [00:12:41] What she did was absolutely standard practice in journalists covering court cases, which is why it was an attack on standard journalistic practice. [00:12:23][24.4]

19. V/O: The Pietermaritzburg High Court agreed.
Karyn: [00:20:20] They went into the merits of Jacob Zuma's case against both myself and Billy Downer, and they eviscerated it on every single point and for a court of law to basically say that this private prosecution is is a an abuse that has been pursued for an ulterior purpose to silence Karen Maughan was was incredibly…gratifying for me because and it made me want to keep doing my job, to keep going
MICAH
20. V/O: The court was just as blunt in the AmaBhungane case
Micah: [00:03:17] It was an excoriating judgment. I mean it just, it absolutely hammered them
Masa: [00:04:16] Judge Sutherland mention nine times that this was an abuse of the court process.
Micah: [00:04:29] It was a very cynical abuse of the court in a desperate attempt to avoid this information being further reported on.

21. V/O: But the fight isn’t over. The Moti Group told us it’s appealing saying “Judges are allowed to get things wrong and appeal courts exist for a reason”

So Amabhungane are strategizing with their lawyers about the next steps to take

LEAD WITH MICAH WALKING THROUGH WEBBER WENTZEL RECEPTION INTO DARIO IN BOARDROOM
Dario: [00:01:48] So we have an application before the Constitutional Court, which we will deal with in due course.
VIZ Dip to black.. open with Karyn and Pieter talking about Zuma’s appeal
22. V/O: Karyn’s legal troubles too.. aren’t over - former President Jacob Zuma is appealing
For now, the courts held the line FOR Media Freedom … but with battle lines drawn, the struggle continues
LINKS AND PROMOS:

PROMO 1:
MASA: Freedom of the press is one of the cornerstones of South Africa’s democracy and the courts are meant to protect this. So what happens when they are instead used to intimidate and harass journalists?

Pieter: [00:06:06] Press freedom in South Africa is always under pressure. They're using deep pockets with lots of resources to try and stop not only stop us from publishing, but try and take us out of the game,

PROMO 2:
MASA: For decades brave journalists have dared to speak truth to power but now they’re faced with having to defend themselves on a new front: criminal court.

Pieter: [00:01:41] This was all about muzzling the media. This was a quite transparent attempt to try and silence a journalist who was simply doing her work.


PROMO 3:
V/O: While the court of public opinion can be vicious…

Karyn: I got so many threats on social media, “You must be raped and murdered and die, bitch, die”, you know, all that kind of stuff.

V/O: Our courts of law have always protected the right to Media Freedom. But for how long?

For over a decade AmaBhungane’s garnered a reputation for hard-hitting exposes by investigative journalists like Micah Reddy. UPSOUND OF MICAH AT DESK ON PHONE Micah 1: [00:00:50] Can you just give me a, uh, a quick kind of briefing on that? 9 V/O: An anonymous source leaked thousands of confidential documents that formed the basis for a series of exposes dubbed #The Moti Files Micah: [00:08:42] A lot of what was in those documents pointed to an improper relationship with the Zimbabwean president and potential fraud and corruption in other areas [00:10:13][27.9] … So these are some of the things that we've explored and there's a lot more to come. [00:11:32][32.9] 10 V/O: Before publishing, AmaBhungane offered the Moti group the right to respond to their allegations. Moti and the Group denied any wrongdoing. They also accused amaBhungane of being in possession of stolen documents. MICAH: We thought they were trying to get at who our source was. And they kept insisting that we hand over the documents. And of course, we wouldn't do that. Source confidentiality is a fundamental principle of journalism. ZUNAID MOTI: It’s important for you to understand that AmaBhungane are liars, they’re part of a theft and they’re trying to cover it up using tabloids that they leaked to 11 V/O: Their refusal to hand back the documents enraged Zunaid Moti. 12 V/O: In June he escalated the fight when they asked a judge to gag AmaBhungane from publishing further exposes. Not only was the request granted, but they were told to return the documents within 48 hours…and shockingly, it all happened “ex parte”. Masa: [00:26:19] What does it mean that it was granted ex parte? [00:26:21][2.2] Micah: [00:26:22] It means that the Moti group went to court secretively without us even knowing and without us being allowed to even present our arguments. Micah: [00:24:39] It was pretty unprecedented in democratic South Africa because it amounts to pre-publication censorship. It's censorship outright 13. V/O: The Moti Group argued that an ex parte interdict was a common mechanism to secure stolen documents ..they argued that AmaBhungane contradicted themselves on whether they in fact had the documents. But for Anton Harber from the Campaign for Free Expression it was a clear example of SLAPP Suit. Anton: [00:14:58] SLAPP stands for strategic litigation against public participation. It's the name that’s been given for cases where the intention is not to seek justice or even to win the case, but to make life difficult for journalists or critics of any sort Anton: [00:03:10] journalists must, in the public interest be able to use leaks that come to them and that the idea of of hearing a case like this ex-parte was outrageous 14. Micah and Nicole having Coffee sequence - let’s try cut it slightly longer 16. V/O: For Micah, the fear of arrest took a toll not just on him but his young family too. Our lawyers had cautioned us. Micah: [00:02:03 nerve-wracking precisely because you were worried not only about your own safety but those of that of people around you. Dip to Black ACT 3 - THE VERDICT 17. V/O: The anxiety was overwhelming as judgement in these two cases loomed… We see Micah Driving Upsound: The Moti Group and AmaBhungane are headed for a legal showdown We see Karyn leaving her house and on her phone Up Sound: Judgement will be handed down today in the private prosecution case against journalist Karyn Maughan 18. V/O:. At stake not just Karyn’s personal liberty but nothing less than the future of media freedom in South Africa. V/O: The court was just as blunt in the AmaBhungane case Micah: [00:03:17] It was an excoriating judgment. I mean it just, it absolutely hammered them Masa: [00:04:16] Judge Sutherland mention nine times that this was an abuse of the court process. metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): What happens when the court system in South Africa is abused to harass journalists, to prevent them from speaking truth to power in an attempt to intimidate them into submission?
metadata.Unique Selling Point: The bill of rights is the cornerstone of South Africa’s democracy. It protects and affirms the values of human dignity, equality and freedom, providing the foundation for the rule of law in this country. Enshrined is the freedom of expression and by extension, the freedom of the press. But what happens when our venerated judicial system, one that is supposed to uphold and protect this inalienable right, is instead weaponised to do the exact opposite? This story looks at 2 powerful case studies showing the exactly how this was done, the personal toll it’s taken on the lives of the journalists involved and the consequences on media freedom in South Africa
metadata.Summary: Karyn Maughn is one of South Africa’s most respected journalists Former President Jacob Zuma launched a private prosecution against her in October - an example of a SLAPP Suit Zuma’s lawyer Dali Mpofu admitted that they did not really have a case but still chose to launch it anyway -Karyn can provide this clip to us If found guilty, she faced up to 15 years in prison The litigation was really expensive. She would not have been able to afford legal representation without the support of News 24 -who supported her throughout and paid for legal counsel. Her editor Pieter Du Toit is a powerful support interview for her story She’s been put through 7 months of hell - the target of a vicious social media campaign against her This led her to withdraw from society, fearing for her safety She left her home and moved back in with her elderly parents for 2 months She’s willing to discuss the mental toll it’s taken on her: she’s no longer the extroverted person she used to be The stress really affected her blood sugar: she’s a type 1 diabetic The case against her was ultimately dismissed in a scathing judgement against Zuma in which he was ordered to pay legal costs too Despite the victory, the intimidation and harassment still continues, as evidenced when she was attacked again by Dali Mpofu at Busisiwe Mkhwebane’s press conference Karyn is willing to admit that in spite of her stoic defence that the ordeal has broken her. She once thought that admitting this would mean that her intimidators had won It’s become all too much for Karyn and she’s going to Denver for a few weeks to escape and recharge. She’s due back on the 18th July Amabhungane is a preeminent investigative unit in SA headed up by veteran journalist Sam Sol They ran a series of exposes on Zunaid Moti’s businesses call the #MotiFiles. These exposes were authored by Dewald Pretorious and Micah Reddy - with Sam acting as a mentor They based their reporting on a number of sources, including a trove of documents that the Moti Group claim to have been stolen In written correspondence from the Moti Group, Amabhungane’s journalists are accused of using stolen documents and threatened with criminal prosecution if they do not return them. At the beginning of June Moti was able to successfully interdict Amabhungane from publishing anymore exposes as well as ordering them to return the “stolen documents” What’s highly unusual is that the order was obtained “ex parte” - meaning the court order was given without knowledge of AmaBhungane Amabhungane argue that returning the documents would reveal their source The case will now be heard in the Johannesburg High Court on Tuesday 27 June. Sam Sole has been subject of a smear campaign launched on Social Media by Zunaid Moti in which he is accused of being an Apartheid spy. His family has been harassed. For example his wife was contacted by a lady claiming to be a journalist and asked about Sam’s time in the army. The “journalist” turned out to be someone working for the Moti Group. Sam, Micah & Dewald have been warned that they face imminent arrest. They fear that Moti has connections with the Sandton Police- though this remains unsubstantiated This feeling of paranoia has led to several occasions in which they’ve had to hurriedly leave home The legal persecution by Moti is another example of SLAPP but Amabhungane don’t have the financial resource like News24 and so could buried by litigation and face the real prospect of bankruptcy.
